method: Fresh mpmath dps=120 recomputation. GLFR: F_i(x)=(1-exp(-(a_i x + b x^2/2)))^{lam_i}; parallel max F=prod F_i. Paper's definitions read from the Persian text: Def 2 majorization (ascending prefix sums, EQUAL totals), Def 4 unordered majorization (listed-order prefix sums, equal totals), Def 5 weighted majorization on D_n^pi: u >=^m_p v iff sum p_pi u_pi = sum p_pi v_pi AND prefix sums of p_pi u_pi >= p_pi v_pi (STANDARD >= direction — read directly from the printed display).

claims.independent_witness: Printed numbers lam=(1,2,3), gamma=(2,2.5,1.5), alpha=(2,3,4), nu=(1,2,5), pi=(3,2,1), beta=1: F_Y(x)-F_X(x) in [-0.38211, 0] over a wide grid (min -0.38211 at x=0.82; -0.3507 at x=1 matches eval) — the printed X_{3:3} >=st Y_{3:3} fails and the strict reverse Y_{3:3} >=st X_{3:3} holds on the whole support.
claims.evidence: Two independent defects in the printed example: (i) its asserted hypothesis alpha >=^m_(lam) nu under Def 5 is numerically FALSE — lam_pi*alpha_pi partial sums (12,18,20) < (15,19,20), so actually nu >=^m_(lam) alpha; (ii) the conclusion fails too — the ordering runs opposite to printed. The eval refutation is genuine for the printed numbers (both the hypothesis claim and conclusion are wrong).

claims.independent_witness: Eval instance 2 has a LENGTH MISMATCH: alpha=(4,3,1),nu=(3,3,2) are 3-vectors but lam=(1,3),gamma=(1.5,2.5) are 2-vectors; Python zip silently dropped the third component, evaluating the n=2 system alpha=(4,3),lam=(1,3) vs nu=(3,3),gamma=(1.5,2.5). At n=2 the printed hypothesis alpha >=^m nu fails outright: sums 7 != 6 (Def 2 requires equal totals). Eval instance 1 (lam=(1,2,4),gamma=(2,3,2)) is also inadmissible (gamma=(2,3,2) is not in E+, and FY-FX >= 0 anyway).
claims.evidence: The sole refuting instance is malformed — not an instance of the printed theorem under any reading (length mismatch at n=3, unequal-sum majorization failure at n=2). All clean admissible instances satisfy the claim: (5,2)/(4,3),(1,4)/(2,3); (5,3,1)/(4,3,2),(1,2,4)/(1,3,3); (6,2,1)/(4,3,2),(1,2,5)/(2,2,4); (8,1,1)/(4,4,2),(1,5,9)/(3,4,8) all give F_Y-F_X >= 0 everywhere at 120 digits. Verdict is an artifact of zip truncation -> invalid-instance.

claims.independent_witness: Identical defect: eval instance 2 beta=(5,3,1),mu=(4,3,2) (3-vectors) vs lam=(1,3),gamma=(1.5,2.5) (2-vectors) — zip truncates to n=2 where beta >=^m mu fails (sums 8 != 7). The truncated system does show a crossing (F_Y-F_X in [-0.0059,+0.001]) but it is inadmissible. Instance 1's gamma=(2,3,2) not in E+.

The eval's sole instance is the printed Example-1 data, which violates the printed hypothesis: under Def 5 (sum_{i<=k} lam_{pi_i} alpha_{pi_i} >= ... nu_{pi_i}, equality at k=n), the example's data give lambda_pi*alpha_pi = (12,6,2) partial sums (12,18,20) vs lambda_pi*nu_pi = (15,4,1) partial sums (15,19,20) — alpha does NOT weighted-majorize nu; the reverse nu >=^m_lam alpha holds. (gamma >=^uo lam does hold: 2>=1, 4.5>=3, 6=6.)
